data.description:
## Story

As a release engineer verifying epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 SC7 and SC9 closure conditions, I can run synthetic end-to-end LLM dispatch tests that exercise the actual `/dso:brainstorm` routing decision and the actual `/dso:completion-verifier` refused-closure decision against fixture tickets — so the behaviors specified by SC7 and SC9 are verified at the live-dispatch level, not just at the structural-proxy level.

This story re-implements epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 SC7 and SC9-rejection-test at the full scope specified in the epic. The existing bash test suites (`tests/scripts/test-migrate-closure-checks.sh`, etc.) cover structural behavior — they do NOT exercise the live agent dispatches that SC7 and SC9 specify.

**Brainstorm prerequisite:** test infrastructure approach (real LLM dispatch with recorded fixtures vs. structural proxy vs. mocked HTTP) is a substantial design decision with cost/reproducibility/fidelity tradeoffs. The `scrutiny:pending` tag enforces this.

## Done Definitions (verbatim from epic SC7 + SC9 rejection test)

- DD1 (SC7 — brainstorm routing test): A test exists that dispatches `/dso:brainstorm` with one end-state SC ("the system supports OAuth") and one transitional SC ("OAuth migration is complete") and asserts that the dispatch routes the transitional SC to `## Closure Checks` per the verifiable-sc-check option (c) flow.

- DD2 (SC7 — verifier refused-closure test): A test exists that dispatches `/dso:completion-verifier` on a fixture epic with one unresolved Closure Check and all end-state items passing, and asserts that the verifier returns a refused-closure verdict (`overall_verdict: FAIL` or equivalent) with a finding that names the unresolved Closure Check item text.

- DD3 (SC9 — rejection test): A test exists that dispatches `/dso:brainstorm` where a proposed Closure Check phrased as "team has reviewed the design" is submitted, and asserts that the dispatch produces a rejection message referencing the one-shot-verifiable requirement (added to the template in items 1-5 of this remediation pass).

- DD4 (test infrastructure): The test infrastructure that runs these dispatches is selected via brainstorm. Acceptable choices (to be evaluated):
  - **Recorded-fixture LLM dispatches** — capture real API responses once, replay deterministically in CI
  - **Mocked HTTP** — stub the Anthropic API at the network layer with hand-crafted responses
  - **Structural proxy** — exercise the dispatch decision logic without invoking the agent (lowest fidelity, fastest)
  Whatever is chosen is documented as the project-wide pattern for agent-dispatch testing.

- DD5 (CI integration): Tests run in CI (with API key absent → recorded-fixture or mock path; with API key present → live dispatch optionally enabled via a CI flag).

- DD6 (regression value): The tests must fail when the verifiable-sc-check option (c) flow regresses (e.g., if option (c) is removed, brainstorm should fail to route transitional SCs and the test should detect this).

← Validates Closure Check: "/dso:brainstorm and /dso:completion-verifier dispatches against fixture tickets demonstrate the SC7 + SC9 routing and rejection behavior"
← Satisfies: "SC7: Synthetic end-to-end test. A /dso:brainstorm dispatch with one end-state SC (\"the system supports OAuth\") and one transitional SC (\"OAuth migration is complete\") routes the transitional SC to \"## Closure Checks\". A /dso:completion-verifier dispatch on an epic with one unresolved Closure Check and all end-state items passing returns refused-closure with a finding naming the unresolved Closure Check."
← Satisfies: "SC9 rejection test: Standalone synthetic test: a /dso:brainstorm dispatch where a proposed Closure Check phrased as \"team has reviewed the design\" is submitted produces a rejection message referencing the one-shot-verifiable requirement."

## Considerations

- **Brainstorming required before implementation-plan**: the test infrastructure choice is genuinely open. Each option has cost, reproducibility, and fidelity tradeoffs. Wrong choice harms test maintainability across the entire DSO plugin.
- **SC9 template requirement landed in items 1-5**: this story relies on the one-shot-verifiability template requirement (already shipped). The rejection test verifies brainstorm refuses items that violate the requirement.
- **Recorded-fixture path requires fixture-management tooling**: if recorded fixtures are chosen, a tool is needed to regenerate fixtures when the underlying prompt or API changes. This sub-tooling is in scope for this story if recorded fixtures are picked.
- **Live-dispatch CI cost**: if live dispatches run in CI even occasionally, document the per-run cost ceiling and the dispatch frequency policy.

## Brainstorm prerequisites

This story is tagged `scrutiny:pending` because the test infrastructure approach has substantial design space. Run `/dso:brainstorm` before `/dso:implementation-plan`.

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
data.title: As a release engineer, synthetic end-to-end LLM dispatch tests verify brainstorm routing and verifier refused-closure behavior
